{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Péter Halász ( August 20, 1943 in Budapest – March 9, 2006 in New York City) was a Hungarian actor and director.","title":"Péter Halász (actor)"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" In 1993 he won the Hungarian Film Critics award for Best Actor.","title":"Péter Halász (actor)"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" He founded several theater companies in Budapest and New York City including the Kassák Studió, the \"appartement theatre\", Squat Theater, Love Theater and Varosi Szinhaz.","title":"Péter Halász (actor)"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" As an actor, he appeared in \"Fat Man and Little Boy\" (1989), \"Sunshine\" (1999), and \"The Breed\" among others.","title":"Péter Halász (actor)"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" In February, 2006 his terminal liver cancer led to his final performance, which involved lying in an open coffin in a Budapest art museum.","title":"Péter Halász (actor)"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" He died a month after this, at the age of 62.","title":"Péter Halász (actor)"},{"sentence_id":6,"text":" He had four children: Judith Halasz, Cora Fisher, Gabor Halasz, and David Halasz.","title":"Péter Halász (actor)"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Meet the Navy was a musical revue produced by the Royal Canadian Navy during World War II.","title":"Meet the Navy"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" Directed by Hollywood producer Louis Silver and Broadway choreographer Larry Ceballos, the production premiered in a private performance for servicemen on 2 September 1943 at Toronto's Victoria Theatre.","title":"Meet the Navy"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The first performance open to the public was given on the following 4 September.","title":"Meet the Navy"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" The production toured Canada in 1943-1944, entertaining approximately a half-million Canadians.","title":"Meet the Navy"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" It then toured to 11 cities in England, and to cities in Wales and Ireland in 1944-1945; beginning in Glasgow on 23 October 1944 and ending at the Hippodrome, London on 7 April 1945.","title":"Meet the Navy"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" The show subsequently toured to the Théâtre Marigny in Paris, the Vauxhall, Brussels, and the Carré Theatre in Amsterdam's Carré.","title":"Meet the Navy"},{"sentence_id":6,"text":" The production's final performance was on 12 September 1945 at the Oldenburgisches Staatstheater in Germany.","title":"Meet the Navy"},{"sentence_id":7,"text":" The National Film Board of Canada produced a documentary \"Meet the Navy on Tour\", and British National Films presented another feature film called \"Meet the Navy\" which was filmed in November 1945 in Britain and released in 1946.","title":"Meet the Navy"},{"sentence_id":8,"text":" Although plans for a Broadway run were made, they never materialized.","title":"Meet the Navy"}],"peer_messages":["Unverified peer answer: noanswer"],"previous_answer":"noanswer","question":"What actor had his final performance in the film based on a dytopian novel by David Eggers called The Circle?"}
